title: Protocol to generate murine organotypic brain cultures for drug screening and evaluation of anti-metastatic efficacy
protocol: Embed brain in 4% low melting agarose preheated at 42°C.
Immerse brain in the mold filled with 4% agarose.
Ensure full coverage of the brain surface with agarose by gently stirring the melted agarose around the brain.
Place the mold on ice.
Gently position the brain in a coronal position using the tip with the region of most interest upwards.
Allow the agarose to solidify.
Section the edges and walls of the mold with a razor blade to extract the agarose block.
Trim excess agarose with a razor blade carefully, ensuring no part of the brain is exposed.
Fixate the trimmed agarose block containing the brain to the sample holder using instant adhesive glue.
Place the sample holder inside the buffer tray.
Fill the buffer tray with ice-cold HBSSsup.
Surround the buffer tray with ice to keep it cold.
Place half of a double-edge razor in the razor-holding arm of the vibratome.
Fix the settings on the control panel for speed, frequency, and slice thickness.
Set the speed to 2 mm/s.
Set the frequency to 5 Hz.
Set the thickness of the slices to 250 μm.
Move the sectioning arm using the forward-reverse option in the control panel.
Select the continuous mode (Cont) on the control panel.
Press Start to begin automatic sectioning.
Collect brain slices with a spatula.
Divide each coronal slice into two halves with a needle tip.
Keep brain slices in a 10 cm plate with ice-cold HBSSsup and on ice.
Transfer halves of the coronal brain slices to a 24-well plate with HBSSsup.
Pipette 1 ml of HBSSsup per well.
Place one brain slice per well.
Add 20 μL of D-luciferin (15 mg/mL) per mL of HBSSsup, gently shake the plate to mix.
Incubate the plate for 5 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Acquire BLI images at exposure times of 10 and 1 second.
Measure the BLI signal of each brain slice using Living Image 4.5 software.
Categorize BLI positive brain slices as having high, medium, or low signals.
Prepare 12-well plates with slice culture medium (SCM) and chemical compounds of interest.
Mix SCM with appropriate volume of chemical compound to achieve desired final concentration for each treatment condition.
Prepare the mix for the corresponding control condition (i.e., SCM + vehicle).
Add 1 mL of mix per well in a 12-well plate.
Place one 0.8 μm pore membrane per well on top of the liquid with the matte side upwards.
Transfer BLI positive brain slices from a 24-well plate to a 10 cm plate with ice-cold HBSSsup using a spatula.
Annotate the well of origin in the 24-well plate and the well where it is plated in the 12-well plate.
Collect one brain slice at a time with a spatula and gently place it on top of a membrane in the 12-well plate.
Repeat until all wells are completed.
Avoid wrinkles in the slices during transfer.
Gently transfer the plate to a CO2 incubator ensuring all membranes (with their respective slices) are floating.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 72 hours.
Refresh SCM in cultures by removing old medium at day 3 without using a vacuum pump.
Gently add new medium on the walls of the wells to avoid wetting the upper surface of the membranes.
Add 20 μL of D-luciferin (15 mg/mL) per mL of SCM in the 12-well plate for BLI.
Gently shake the plate to mix after adding D-luciferin.
Incubate the plate for 5 minutes before BLI acquisition.
Acquire BLI images at exposure times of 10 seconds and 1 second.
If higher exposure times were used at day 0 BLI (30, 60, or 120 seconds), acquire additional images at the corresponding exposure times.
Remove SCM from organotypic cultures.
Add 1 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde to each well.
Shake overnight at 4 degrees Celsius for a minimum of 12 hours.
Remove 4% paraformaldehyde and wash three times with 1× PBS.
Store fixed organotypic cultures in 1× PBS at 4 degrees Celsius.
For long-term storage, maintain fixed organotypic cultures in 0.25% sodium azide (in 1× PBS) at 4 degrees Celsius.
Replace liquid periodically to avoid drying up.
Add 4% paraformaldehyde through the wall of each well and not on top of the organotypic cultures.
Use a tip to push the membrane with the slice into the liquid to ensure full submergence.
